claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first assessment question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is/are your child/children?**

Please tell me:
- The name and age of each child you're inquiring about

This is important because eligibility depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify
- **16-19**: Need to be in education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Once you provide these details, I can guide you through the rest of the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 16 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check whether they're in education or training, or if they qualify under other extension criteria. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to find out about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in education or training, has they recently left education, or neither?**

To help clarify:
- **In education or training**: This includes secondary school, sixth form, college, university, or approved training schemes
- **Recently left education**: If Alex left education within the last 20 weeks, there may be extension eligibility
- **Neither**: If Alex has been out of education for more than 20 weeks and isn't doing any training

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - they're doing their A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in education doing A-levels at sixth form college. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check some details about Alex's A-level course to make sure it qualifies:

**A few questions about Alex's A-level education:**

1. **How many hours per week is Alex studying?** (Child Benefit requires at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

2. **Is this A-level course funded by their employer or is it an employer-agreed arrangement for a future job?** (These types wouldn't qualify)

3. **Is Alex married?** (If so, they would need to be financially dependent on you to qualify)

A-levels are generally approved education, so as long as the study is at least 12 hours per week and isn't employer-funded, Alex should be on track to qualify!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
1. Yes, Alex is doing full-time A-levels - it's definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study.

2. No, this isn't funded by an employer - it's just regular sixth form college.

3. No, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex meets all the criteria for approved education. Now let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is in full-time education, many students work part-time. The key is that they're not working 24+ hours per week. If Alex is not working at all or working less than 24 hours per week, they'll meet this requirement.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're just focused on their studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't work at all, so they meet this requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any specific benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(These benefits would make them ineligible for Child Benefit)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name - they're still dependent on me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is in an apprenticeship:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Most apprenticeships would disqualify them, with the exception of Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales (which are approved). However, since Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form, I expect the answer is no - but I want to confirm to make sure there's no apprenticeship element involved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - just the A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now let me move to the next check, which is about your residency.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. There are several possible paths that could qualify you:

**Which of the following best describes your situation:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If so, you'd need to meet additional criteria (working, seeking work, have sufficient resources, studying, or are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** - In certain qualifying countries

For most people, the answer will be that you normally live in the UK. Can you confirm which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirement. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. There are a few ways this can be satisfied:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** - You're the main carer/live together
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for their food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc. at least equivalent to Child Benefit (or provide equivalent in kind)
3. **You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement** - You make payments towards Alex's maintenance that cover their upkeep

Since Alex is 16 and still in education, I'd expect you're living with them and providing their main care. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me - I'm their main carer.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex and are their main carer, so you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person who might claim?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also potentially claiming?
- Are you and Alex's other parent in agreement about who should claim?
- Or is there a dispute about who should be the main claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only potential claimant for Alex. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In hospital** - Receiving inpatient hospital treatment
2. **In care** - In a children's home or other local authority care
3. **Fostered** - In a foster care arrangement
4. **Living normally** - At home or in their normal living arrangement (e.g., student accommodation if at university)

Since Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form and living with you, I expect the answer is that they're living normally. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex is just living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now for the final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

This is asking whether your local council (in Manchester) is providing financial support for Alex's housing or upkeep. For most families where the child lives at home with their parents, the answer would be no. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me provide you with your final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me confirm your eligibility outcome with all the details.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit

**For: Alex (age 16)**

---

### Summary

You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

✅ **Alex's circumstances:**
- In full-time approved education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- Studying more than 12 hours per week
- Not working 24+ hours per week
- Not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
- Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- Living with you at home

✅ **Your circumstances:**
- Normally resident in the UK (Manchester)
- Responsible for Alex (main carer, living together)
- Only potential claimant for Alex
- Local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

---

### Next Steps

To claim Child Benefit, you'll need to:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay back some or all of the benefit through tax

**Payment schedule:** Child Benefit is normally paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits).

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations, and best of luck with your claim!

You are normally resident in the UK (Manchester), you are responsible for Alex (living with them and providing care), no other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, Alex is living normally at home, and the local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.

You have met all the claimant requirements including residency in the UK and financial responsibility for Alex.">
